about.title: Brentwood Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it hurts someone — a faulty ladder rung gives out, a power tool's guard fails, a household appliance shorts and starts a fire. Brentwood households, with its mix of newer subdivisions and working ranch properties near Balfour Road and Sand Creek Road, use plenty of tools, vehicles, and consumer goods every day, and any of them can carry a hidden defect. California law gives injured people a real advantage here: strict liability generally means you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That covers design flaws, manufacturing mistakes, and inadequate warnings alike, and liability can extend to distributors and retailers, not just the maker. If a product hurt you or someone in your family in Brentwood, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, to look at what happened and what the law allows.

whyChoose.title: Why Brentwood Residents Look Into This

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Burden
items.desc: Because California generally applies strict liability to defective products, you often don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the defect existed and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which matters if a product passed through several hands before reaching your Brentwood home.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the item exactly as it was after the injury helps an attorney evaluate whether a design, manufacturing, or warning defect contributed to what happened.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try not to repair, discard, or alter it in any way. Store it safely along with packaging, manuals, and receipts if you have them. This evidence can be important to an attorney assessing your claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability rules for defective products generally focus on whether the product itself was unreasonably dangerous, not on the manufacturer's state of mind. An attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Is this only about products bought or used in Brentwood?
items.answer: No — the location of purchase doesn't determine liability, but if the injury happened in Brentwood or Contra Costa County, that can affect where a claim is filed. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can explain what applies to your case.
